facts.text: Norwood Park got its name from Henry Ward Beecher’s 1868 novel 'Norwood,' but the 'Park' was added when another Illinois town already used Norwood.
The Noble–Seymour–Crippen House, built in 1833, stands as Chicago’s oldest extant building and a centerpiece of Norwood Park’s historic district.
In 1986 Chicago declared the Norwood Park Historic District, and in 1988 the Noble–Seymour–Crippen House became a city landmark.
Norwood Park’s strong Polish heritage has attracted new Polish immigrants in recent years, enriching the neighborhood’s cultural tapestry.
Union Ridge, one of Cook County’s highest points, borders Norwood Park and offers scenic views that have drawn visitors for generations.
William Howard Taft High School, completed in 1939, inspired the 1978 musical Grease and remains a local landmark.
